text: The results hold at their stated scopes, including explicit repairs; they do not prove every unrestricted historical formulation or any physical application.
No single finite model carries both strict live-overlap lineage and all eight conditions at design grade.
The ancestry-based certificates are at different checkpoints; we do not claim that the source package, the children and the fused output coexist.

On the strict-continuation instances, conditions (4)-(7) hold only in simplified form: a single collision instead of full non-exposure, a declared credit rule, a declared event order and record lift, and a declared coupling.
On the model that computes all eight conditions, condition (4) is privacy for the current family of observations on maintained support only, not full privacy.

Disturbances are limited to the declared classes: nominal disturbances with all positive branches in the strict handoff, and unit disturbances with retained renewable ports on the ancestry model. Arbitrary resource shocks, external destruction and maintenance with no supply are not covered.
Generated historical source and birth archives can remain after withdrawal; neither source-memory erasure nor numerical identity is inferred.

The ancestry result rests on two readings the author adopted. The first is completed local-cycle evidence with continuously authenticated current residency and mandatory bridges to the current generator, ownership and control, in place of the original admission rule. The second is a finite certificate with nonempty, universal full-history lifting, in place of finite enumeration of growing histories.
The selected-response sparse format used in the strict handoff is representation-sensitive.

For the defined game semantics, autonomy is equivalent to the existence of a proof-bearing invariant certificate; this is a semantic existence result, not a search procedure. The finite-factor constructor is sound but potentially incomplete: its failure to produce a certificate does not show that autonomy fails.
In the strict handoff, autonomy acquisition uses historical source support, while lineage uses funded actual source execution.

On the ancestry model, the stationarity and uniqueness checks for condition (1) concern the finite physical matrix. Growing history records are excluded from the stationarity claim, and a period-two two-step counterexample to a stronger uniqueness gate is retained.
On the ancestry model, full future laws including the initial observation, and branch emissions after actions, are distinct readouts; neither is substituted for the other.
The greatest operational viable set includes cold charged residents. The greatest autonomy set that preserves the package is separate, and restricts competitors to the adopted acceptance condition.
A freshly fused output is charged but does not yet satisfy the conditions; it qualifies only after its own acquisition.
The flatness license used is the stronger adopted one (completion ranks and a shared unique normal form), not boundary equality alone.
The POS-04 instance of finite-horizon autonomy is derived by projecting the historical runtime to a finite factor; the frozen model data alone do not supply it.
In the package-preserving version of the strict theorem, autonomy implies realization by construction; only the operational version proves the three conclusions logically independent.
The two temporal hypotheses about felt time and felt continuity are hypotheses, not conclusions of any result.
Realizing the conditions on a target is neither lineage nor soundness of any consciousness certificate.
Strict lineage is not numerical identity and does not assert phenomenal continuity.
Direct succession is not substituted into strict continuation and is not personal survival.
Autonomy is model-relative and does not establish indefinite physical resource availability.
Endpoint equality does not create a canonical global present.
No scalar score, empirical noise model or open-ended robustness theorem is supplied.
Nothing here shows that any measurement of a real system identifies these predicates.
Substrate Indifference, personal survival and numerical identity are not established by any result.
Transport between systems does not establish lineage, consciousness or substrate indifference.
We do not argue that consciousness can or cannot move between substrates.
No system, biological, artificial or hypothetical, is certified as conscious.
Personal identity is not decided by stipulation.
Passing between finite systems of different types is not Substrate Indifference; no invariance theorem across substrates is given.
An exact copy is not a unique continuation; symmetric duplication leaves the verdict underdetermined without an extra premise.
Passing a certificate is not the same as the certificate being sound.
Exact finite results are not generalized to noisy, large or continuous systems.
Reconstruction after the source becomes inactive is distinguished from preservation; the source's records are retained, so it is not total erasure.
Words such as transfer, upload, same person, survival and transcendence appear only as informal framing or in reports of others' views, never as a result's conclusion.
The record arrow is a structural ordering by record growth; it is not a path-reversal or thermodynamic arrow of time.
Six Birds corpus statements are provenance for the design, cited in the versions the design read; several were revised later, and no result here depends on any of them.
Lean checks the stated declarations; agreement between the prose statements and the Lean statements is checked by review (W18), not by the kernel.

On the two-copy model the target's copy of the deadline system is given in advance and is latent until a mixed event activates it; the receiver copies the source's terminal raw position and phase at that event. This is a designed transfer rule, not incremental construction of the target's organization and not independent causal corroboration.
